claude.sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

links.outcome: Hallucinations and clinical terminology errors in ASR transcripts
links.effect: Hallucinations absent except Whisper (n=57) and DigitalTCO (n=1); clinically significant errors seen with all systems, ranging 2% to 66%.
links.quote: Hallucinations were absent except for Whisper (n = 57) and DigitalTCO (n = 1).

links.outcome: Clinically significant transcription errors that would require verification
links.effect: Clinically significant errors seen with all systems, ranging from 2% to 66% (GPT4oTranscribeCorrected clean; Dragon Medical One background noise).
links.quote: Importantly, clinically significant errors were seen with all systems, ranging from 2% to 66% (GPT4oTranscribeCorrected clean; Dragon Medical One background noise, respectively).

links.outcome: ASR accuracy under background noise and narrator accent variation
links.effect: Background noise increased DWER and WER (P<0.001); accent had no effect in clean conditions (P=0.65) and small effect with noise (P=0.001).
links.quote: Across systems, background noise increased DWER and WER (P < 0.001).

links.outcome: Comparative transcription accuracy across 10 ASR systems on same data
links.effect: GPT4oTranscribeCorrected best (DWER 3.5%; WER 3.7%); Heidi Health best commercial (DWER 6.2%); Dragon Professional Anywhere worst (WER 33.9%).
links.quote: Heidi Health was the highest-performing commercial system (DWER = 6.2%; WER = 5.4%), with Dragon Professional Anywhere being the worst (WER = 33.9%).

unlisted_practices: LLM-based generative error correction of ASR transcripts to reduce clinical terminology errors

links.effect: Clinically significant errors ranged from 2% to 66% across systems/conditions.

links.effect: Hallucinations were absent except for Whisper (n=57) and DigitalTCO (n=1).

links.effect: Best system had DWER=3.5%, WER=3.7%; DWER decreased 54.9% versus GPT4oTranscribe.

screen.practice: LLM-based generative error correction of ASR transcripts
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates whether adding a downstream LLM generative error correction stage to an existing speech recognition tool (GPT4oTranscribe vs GPT4oTranscribeCorrected) mitigates transcription errors and hallucinations.
